newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares to hover around 2,700, watching U.S..
newsitem.headline: German shares to hover around 2,700, watching U.S..

text.p: German shares were expected to continue to consolidate over the coming days and hover around the record high levels reached in the last few weeks.
The IBIS DAX electronic trade index was down 6.66 points at 2,698.99. The DAX closed down 11.47 points at 2,691.17.
After so many consecutive record highs, dealers said a period of consolidation was a healthy sign and said the day's weakness was not the beginning of a reversal.
"We can slide a little bit or move sideways over the next few days and then take another run up beyond 2,700 points," said one trader.
"The market is holding itself well at these high levels," said one trader.
Dealers said they would look to Wall Street to provide direction, although the Dow Jones index was also seen to be consolidating just below the 6,000 mark.
"The Americans must also decide in which direction we are heading," said one trader. "Until the U.S. election we expect the market to continue to be positive."
Dealers said the German market was also awaiting the release of U.S. retail sales and producer price data scheduled for Friday.

Metals group Metallgesellschaft AG was the day's best performer in the DAX, gaining over four percent after saying profits for the 1995/1996 financial year would top the previous year. In post-bourse dealings, MG shares rose as high as 1.65 marks to 28.90 marks.
MG officials said the firm had done "extraordinarily well" under difficult conditions.

Sportswear manufacturer Adidas jumped 6.10 marks in pre-bourse trade to a new high at 148 marks after announcing it will be an official sponsor for the 1998 soccer World Cup. Adidas was up 4.50 at 146.40 marks in IBIS dealings.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa also moved against the trend, hitting 224.90 marks in pre-bourse dealings after it said a co-operative alliance with Scandinavian airline SAS would improve its net earnings by 100 million marks in 1997.
Lufthansa shares later pared some of the gains to trade up two marks at 224.00 marks in post-bourse IBIS dealings.
